newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: DOWNER RECEIVES ASSURANCE OVER NUCLEAR SHIPMENT
Foreign Affairs Minister, Alexander Downer, has received assurances that a shipment of re-processed nuclear waste being transported from France to Japan meets international safety standards.
Greenpeace says leaked documents indicate the ship, which left the French port of Cherbourg two days ago, will travel through the Tasman sea on its way to Japan.
The environment group expects it to pass Australia in late February, but not to enter the 360 kilometre exclusive economic zones.
A spokesman for Mr Downer says the minister has received safety assurances from the governments of France and Japan, and the minister appears satisfied with the response.
In contrast, the New Zealand Foreign Minister, Don McKinnon has lodged a protest with the Japanese Government over the shipment.
ACTING PM SAYS WIK ISSUE A BIG ONE FOR '97
Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer says the Government wants a clear decision as soon as possible on what will happen with pastoral leases in the future.

Mr Fischer, who's on a tour of rural communities in New South Wales and Queensland to hear views on the High Court's Wik ruling, says the ruling will be one of the most important issues for the Government this year.
The acting Prime Minister says the Wik ruling affects all landholders, not just those in Queensland where the matter was originally raised.
But he says the Government wants to provide a consistent response to all parties.
ONE BODY FOR AIR AND SEA RESCUES PLANNED
A centralised body is to take over the co-ordination of all air and sea rescues in Australia, in an effort to improve communication during rescues.
The air rescue service, Air Services Australia, will close its Melbourne and Brisbane operations, and be incorporated into the new five million dollar national Search and Rescue Centre in Canberra.
The national centre will be managed by the Maritime Safety Authority.
Federal Transport Minister John Sharp says the change will make rescues faster and better, and will be effective from July.
REDFERN POLICE DEFEND TACTICS
Police have denied using heavy-handed tactics during an incident in Sydney's Redfern area yesterday, where a large contingent of police officers were sent in to search for suspected bag snatchers.
The Minister for Police, Paul Whelan, has called for a report into the incident.
Redfern Police Commander Kevin Rafferty says 35 officers were sent to the Eveleigh Street area as part of a planned operation.
The operation followed an earlier incident, where two detectives were allegedly pelted with bricks and bottles while searching for a 19-year-old who'd escaped from custody.
Inspector Rafferty says the large police presence was necessary for the officers protection.
MINERALS COUNCIL SAYS SMALL GOLD PRODUCERS WILL SUFFER
The Northern Territory Minerals Council says small gold producers could suffer as a result of the drop in gold prices, because they're more likely to have higher costs.
The price of gold hit a three-year low last week and continued its slide in New York overnight, trading at US$353.45 an ounce, down $3.80 on yesterday's Sydney close.

Chairman of the Council's gold producers committee, Graham Ehm, says with an Australian dollar price of 450 an ounce, there'll be sustained pressure on the margins of small producers producing over the 400-dollar an ounce level.
WA ENTRY IN ROUND THE WORLD RACE IMPOUNDED
Western Australia's entry in this year's Whitbread round-the-world yacht race has been impounded in Sydney after having an arrest warrant slapped on it by a former skipper.
The 18-metre, "Elle Racing" has been chained up in Darling harbour after Adrienne Cahalan claimed 94 thousand dollars unpaid wages from the syndicate.
Cahalan, two other crew members and the shore manager quit the project earlier this month, claiming they weren't being paid.
Her action will resume in the federal court in Sydney this morning.
The West Australian government has put up 400 thousand dollars sponsorship for the entry as part of a million dollar deal with Elle Mcpherson to promote tourism.
JENNER TO CHECK OUT WARNE
Australian leg-spinner Shane Warne will go under the watchful eye of former Test spinner Terry Jenner in the lead-up to next week's fourth Test against the West Indies.
Jenner will be at the Australian practice session in Melbourne this morning to offer words of advice to Warne as he searches for his elusive form.
In his last two matches Warne has been handled with ease by the West Indies batsmen, in particular champion left-hander Brian Lara.
However, Jenner says there's no need for great concern at the moment.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
